claim_text: Field surveys put the onset of hail damage at 1.00 in for three-tab asphalt shingles and 1.25 in for laminated shingles (all ages).
permitted_inference: Onset (5%) of the laminated-shingle band at 1.25 in; three-tab 1.0 in as the high case.
prohibited_inference: Read the onset as the size at which every roof is replaced.
reasoning: Two Haag-linked tables agree; based on hundreds of inspected roofs and decades of tests.
update_trigger: A US claims study by roof type and hail size.

claim_text: Freezer ice stones at free-fall speed, perpendicular impacts: 11-year-old laminated shingles were damaged by 0/0/60/90/100% of impacts at 1/1.25/1.5/1.75/2.0 in; 11-year-old three-tab fiberglass shingles by 0/60/90/100/100%.
exact_locator: p. 3 Table 2; p. 2 (test ice harder than natural hail; perpendicular = worst case)
permitted_inference: Full-damage (95%) size of the laminated band at 2.0 in; the reference roof (10 years) matches the 11-year test age.
prohibited_inference: Read the impact percentages as roof replacement probabilities.
reasoning: Lab impacts are a worst case (hard ice, square-on), so the band sits at or above the lab points: the curve gives 36% at 1.5 in where 60% of lab impacts damaged.

claim_text: Roofing damage means a diminished water-shedding capability or a reduced expected life (shingle punctures, tears, mat fractures, granules displaced to expose the bitumen); granule loss alone is not functional damage.
exact_locator: S001 p. 3 §4a; S002 text; S013 text
permitted_inference: Count only functional (physical) damage that requires repair.
prohibited_inference: Count cosmetic marks or denting as damage.
reasoning: Matches the real-damage-only choice (D-HRE-05) and the reviewer's request to separate cosmetic denting.

claim_text: Smallest hail sizes that damage low-slope coverings: thermoplastic single-ply membranes 1 to 2 in; EPDM 2 in; steel panels 2 1/2 in (hard hail, perpendicular impacts, average support, good or midlife roofs).
exact_locator: Figure 'Hail thresholds for low-slope roof coverings'
parameter_or_rule: office roof band; warehouse roof onset
permitted_inference: Office TPO band 1.0-2.0 in read as 5%-95%; warehouse onset 2.5 in.
prohibited_inference: Read the range as a stated probability interval.
reasoning: The range reflects membrane thickness, age and support; it is the only public TPO threshold found.
update_trigger: A TPO hail test series by age and attachment.

claim_text: Metal panels in good to fair condition need hail of at least 2.5 in to rupture; dents on seam tops are not an open seam; insurers write cosmetic-damage exclusions.
exact_locator: S003 web article; S004 web page (metal cosmetic damage from 1.5 in)
permitted_inference: Warehouse functional onset 2.5 in; cosmetic denting from 1.5 in only as the alternative case.
prohibited_inference: Treat 2.5 in as the size at which every panel ruptures.
reasoning: Two engineering sources agree; no source gives the upper end, so full damage at 3.5 in is judgment (HRE-C021).
update_trigger: Haag 2010 report or a metal-panel hail test with sizes above 2.5 in.

claim_text: Single-ply membranes can be damaged by hail of 1.5 in or more; walls have no industry hail rating; glazing is susceptible (no size given).
parameter_or_rule: cross-check; wall and window evidence gap
permitted_inference: Cross-check the TPO band; record that wall and window thresholds are judgment.
prohibited_inference: Use the brief as a measured window or siding threshold.
reasoning: Independent engineering firm; consistent with HRE-C004.

claim_text: Aged (up to 20-30-year equivalence) fully adhered 60-mil TPO on a high-density polyiso cover board was not punctured by 2 in ice balls unless struck over a fastener; cover boards cracked at 20-year equivalence after three impacts.
permitted_inference: Low case for the office: membrane band 1.5-2.0 in.
prohibited_inference: Assume the reference office is adhered on a cover board (attachment unstated).
reasoning: A robust assembly sits at the top of the Haag range; the profile does not state attachment or cover board.
update_trigger: Hazard states the TPO attachment and cover board.

claim_text: Hazus default one-storey residential subassembly cost ratios: roofing 3% of building cost; repair work costs 1.25 times new work (repair-and-remodel factor).
permitted_inference: House roof cover share = 3% x 1.25 = 3.75% of structure replacement cost new.
prohibited_inference: Read the Hazus economy-house ratio as exact for the reference house.
reasoning: FEMA's published ratio; implies about $685 per 100 ft2 roofing square on the $405,000 house, a realistic 2025 replacement price. The Hazus house has a 4:12 roof of 14 squares; the reference house has 22.2 squares (not rescaled).
update_trigger: A published US cost model by component.

claim_text: Hazus replaces the whole asphalt roof covering once more than 0.5% of it is damaged.
permitted_inference: A damaged roof is replaced whole (the curve's y-axis is the chance of whole-cover replacement).
prohibited_inference: Apply the hurricane damage state to hail.
reasoning: Hail spreads hits over the whole roof; FEMA's costing replaces the whole cover at a low damaged share.

claim_text: Hazus three-storey motel cost ratios: roof covering 1.1%, roof insulation 0.7% (roofing 2.1%); commercial repair factor 1.25 and overhead and profit 1.20.
permitted_inference: Office roof share = (1.1% + 0.7%) x 1.25 x 1.20 = 2.7%: hail-holed TPO lets water into the insulation, which is replaced with it.
prohibited_inference: Read the motel as an office.
reasoning: Same storey count; implies about $16.20/ft2 of roof, realistic for tear-off and new insulation and membrane. Membrane only (1.65%) is the low case.

claim_text: Hazus adjusts commercial roofing cost ratios by storey count: R' = R(1 - 2.2(Nm/N - 1)) for fewer storeys.
permitted_inference: A one-storey motel would carry roofing 2.1% x 2.47 = 5.2% (x 1.5 factors = 7.8%): a floor for the warehouse, whose interiors cost far less than a motel's.
prohibited_inference: Use the motel-derived ratio as the warehouse value.
reasoning: No Hazus warehouse breakdown exists; the warehouse share is judgment (HRE-C022).

claim_text: Reference designs: house asphalt shingles on wood sheathing, 6:12 gable, roof 2,218.18 ft2, vinyl siding, windows 15%; warehouse standing-seam metal, 1:12, roof 100,346.62 ft2, insulated metal walls, windows 2%, eight overhead doors; office TPO on insulated metal deck, roof 18,003.91 ft2, masonry veneer, windows 33%, six rooftop units; roof covers 10 years old; budgets $405,000, $11.0M, $10.8M.
permitted_inference: Bind records and compute areas.

claim_text: Hazard sends mesh_diameter_mm = MESH75 = 15.096 x ((raw/2.54)^2)^0.206 (capped at 203.2 mm) for native pixels with raw MRMS MESH >= 25.4 mm and zero damage elsewhere; MESH75 at raw 25.4 mm is 38.98 mm.
permitted_inference: Axis = mesh_diameter_mm as delivered; Damage reads it as the largest hailstone diameter at the building.
prohibited_inference: Undo MESH75 in Damage; evaluate a cell maximum.
reasoning: MESH75 is a radar estimate of the 75th percentile of reported maximum hail; the roof thresholds are stated in maximum stone size.

claim_text: Swiss insured buildings: mean damage ratio 0.05% (CI 0.02-0.09%) of building value at 60 mm MESHS, with 5% of buildings claiming.
permitted_inference: A portfolio average over all buildings in a 1 km pixel, including unhit ones; about 1% per claiming building.
prohibited_inference: Use as the reference buildings' conditional damage.
reasoning: Different stock (tile roofs, blinds), country, value basis and radar product (D-HRE-01).

claim_text: Asphalt shingles cover about 80% of US homes; repeated sub-severe hail lowers shingle resistance to later large hail.
permitted_inference: The house roof type is the common case; the per-event curve omits cumulative damage.
prohibited_inference: Add a cumulative term.
reasoning: No quantitative basis for a per-event adjustment.

prohibited_inference: Claim the sources state percentiles.
reasoning: Reading as 68% or 95% moves the house roof at 1.5 in between 33% and 41% (central 36%).
